stem: A client scheduled for noncardiac surgery has an elevated Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI). A team member says, ‘This score means the client automatically needs a preoperative stress test.’ Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Agree because any elevated RCRI requires stress testing before noncardiac surgery
options.B: Recognize that RCRI is one validated tool in stepwise perioperative cardiovascular assessment; additional testing depends on the overall clinical picture, functional capacity, surgical risk, and whether testing would change management
options.C: Disregard RCRI because validated risk-prediction tools are no longer used in perioperative assessment
options.D: Interpret RCRI as a diagnostic test for obstructive coronary artery disease rather than a perioperative risk tool

rationale: The 2024 AHA/ACC perioperative guideline recommends stepwise cardiovascular assessment for noncardiac surgery. Validated tools such as RCRI or NSQIP inform decisions but do not diagnose coronary disease or automatically mandate stress testing. Stress testing is reserved for selected patients when perioperative risk is elevated, functional capacity is poor or unknown, and the result would affect management; routine testing in low-risk situations can create unnecessary delay and over-testing.
educational_objective: Use RCRI as one component of stepwise perioperative cardiovascular risk assessment; do not treat an elevated score as an automatic stress-test indication or a diagnosis of coronary disease.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology
source_document_title: 2024 AHA/ACC/ACS/ASNC/HRS/SCA/SCCT/SCMR/SVM Guideline for Perioperative Cardiovascular Management for Noncardiac Surgery
source_locator: ACC Key Points 2-4: stepwise perioperative CV assessment; validated risk-prediction tools including RCRI/NSQIP inform decisions; stress testing only in highly selected patients with poor/unknown functional capacity and elevated risk; no routine stress testing in low-risk settings
source_claim_supported: Current AHA/ACC guidance uses RCRI as a validated perioperative risk tool within broader stepwise assessment and does not make an elevated score an automatic stress-test indication.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — provide preoperative care; identify risk factors/potential complications associated with procedures; interpret significant assessment/testing information
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — perioperative cardiovascular risk assessment
correction_summary: Replaced RCRI-purpose recall with current AHA/ACC stepwise interpretation and removed the implication that a risk score alone determines testing.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Official 2024 AHA/ACC guideline hub/key points verified and current in 2026.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: RCRI as validated risk tool, stepwise assessment and selective stress testing are supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect: elevated RCRI alone does not mandate stress testing.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect: RCRI estimates perioperative risk, not obstructive CAD diagnosis.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B states both purpose and limitation accurately.
audit_findings.cueing: All options interpret the same score.
audit_findings.blueprint: Reduction of Risk Potential retained appropriately.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Exact testing thresholds intentionally omitted; no unsupported numeric rule or second answer remains.
